narrative.summary: Ground Truth review recorded a storage-poisoning path in this extension where a page-controlled custom event on the YouTube origin reaches extension local storage. Static analysis marks the path TRUE_POSITIVE and manual review confirms it, while the dynamic run was inconclusive after exceeding its budget and provides no runtime confirmation.

findings.gtf-eca35cfbe1d2bab3: A script running on a page matching https://www.youtube.com/* can dispatch the custom event `_live_catch_up_video_meta` with an attacker-controlled `detail.channel_id`; the content-script listener at L143 forwards `e.detail` to `onChannelIdUpdate`, where only a truthiness/liveness check is applied before the value reaches `chrome.storage.local.set` at L443. The privilege boundary is the content-script match on YouTube pages, allowing page-controlled input to alter extension-owned storage state; ExPGuard static analysis records TRUE_POSITIVE (confidence 0.6) and manual review records TP (confidence 0.95), while the dynamic run was INCONCLUSIVE_AFTER_DEBUG and did not reproduce the behavior, so no runtime confirmation is claimed.

recommendations: Treat page-dispatched custom events such as `_live_catch_up_video_meta` as untrusted input and prevent `detail.channel_id` from directly selecting or constructing extension-owned storage values.
Validate `channel_id` against the expected YouTube channel ID format and, where feasible, an allowlist; reject non-conforming values instead of writing them.
Write storage updates through a schema that permits only known keys with sanitized values rather than merging arbitrary objects into extension state.
Narrow the content-script match pattern from `https://www.youtube.com/*` to the specific YouTube pages the sync feature actually requires.
Avoid triggering privileged storage writes from page-originated events; obtain the required metadata through extension-owned logic or a background message validated against extension state.
narrative.impact: The recorded impact is limited to poisoning extension local storage through a page-controlled event on pages matching https://www.youtube.com/*, which may affect extension behavior or state that relies on the stored channel ID; it does not imply account compromise, data theft, or malware installation.
